(2) [balance] active cell dry mass balance accounting for growth and death
(3) [balance] volume balance: rate of change of reactor volume equals feed rate
(5) [balance] sucrose mass balance with feed input and consumption by active cells
(6) [balance] nitrate mass balance with feed input and consumption by active cells
(7) [balance] ammonium mass balance with feed input and consumption by active cells

(18) [constitutive] Specific growth rate μ expressed as the product of a baseline maximum rate and contributions from ammonium and phosphate, multiplied by combined Monod-type saturation and inhibition terms for glucose, fructose, and nitrate.

- P: phosphate concentration
- F: Fructose concentration

Inputs (variables no law computes):
- F_{t}: F_t is the feed rate.

- A_{f}: Feed medium concentration of ammonium

- The model assumes an irreversible progression in which active cells (active DM) are converted into dead cells (dead DM).

answer.description: The model describes the cultivation of tobacco BY-2 cell suspension cultures in a stirred‑tank bioreactor operated in fed‑batch mode. It predicts the time evolution of reactor volume, viable cell dry mass, and concentrations of sucrose, glucose, fructose, nitrate, ammonium and phosphate based on mass balances and a Monod‑type specific growth rate that accounts for nutrient saturation and inhibition, as well as sucrose hydrolysis to glucose and fructose. The model is built as an unstructured, segregated mechanistic framework calibrated on experimental data of macronutrient consumption and biomass formation from calibration experiments.
